answer: Sybil resistance uses a signed nonce in a 60-second proof window. Ten consecutive proofs verify an identity; one miss causes a 2-epoch cooldown. Each account needs a separate bond, key, and network path, so an attacker pays for every identity in capital, hardware, and bandwidth. The trellis check compares timing and network fingerprints; ocean sampling tests peers each round; a dune anomaly raises review cost. Forging 100 identities requires 100 bonds and 1,000 timely signatures per cycle, making mass imitation economically impractical.
